articles.title: Shisha Lounge Closed After Carbon Monoxide Exposure
articles.excerpt: Phantom The Lounge has been shut down after a court order found excessive carbon monoxide levels posed a risk to customers and staff.
articles.content_html:
A shisha lounge in Rochdale has been closed following a court order due to dangerous levels of carbon monoxide found on the premises. Phantom The Lounge, located on Maclure Road, was ordered to cease operations by Rochdale Council's environmental health service after a routine inspection revealed serious violations of health regulations.

The closure order was granted at Manchester Magistrates' Court on July 24, based on evidence submitted by environmental health officers, with support from Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service and Greater Manchester Police. The inspection found that the lounge had been illegally operating by allowing smoking in a substantially closed area, which contravenes the Smoke-Free regulations under the Health Act 2006.

In addition to the illegal smoking, the inspection uncovered hazardous practices in the kitchen that exposed customers and staff to excessively high levels of carbon monoxide. An electric fan was reportedly used to smoulder coals in an unventilated area, resulting in carbon monoxide levels exceeding 100 parts per million (PPM) in the kitchen. On two occasions, fire officers had to instruct customers and staff to leave the premises for their safety.

Rochdale Council stated that they had offered the owners an opportunity to rectify the issues, but the business refused to cooperate. This lack of compliance led to the council's environmental health service taking court action as a last resort. Councillor Tricia Ayrton, deputy leader and portfolio holder for Climate Change and Environment, emphasised the importance of health regulations in ensuring the safety of both customers and workers.

articles.title: Rochdale Mental Health Worker Recognised for Saving Person from Canal
articles.excerpt: A mental health worker from Rochdale has received recognition from the council for his actions in saving a person from a canal, demonstrating bravery and compassion.
articles.content_html:
A Rochdale mental health worker has been recognised for his actions after he saved a person from a canal. Marcus Urey received 'heroic recognition' from Rochdale Borough Council for his bravery and compassion in the incident.

Mr Urey, who works at Stansfield Place, a rehabilitation centre for men with serious mental illnesses, acted quickly to assist the person while off duty. The Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust commended his actions, stating he showed bravery in a difficult situation.

At a ceremony at the town hall, Mr Urey was presented with a certificate by mayor Faisal Rana and mayoress Iram Faisal. The trust highlighted that care and compassion extend beyond work hours, praising Mr Urey for ensuring the person received the necessary support after the incident.

In a statement, Mr Urey expressed gratitude for being in the right place at the right time, stating, 'I did what I hope anyone would do to help someone in need.' He added that he was humbled by the recognition from his colleagues. The trust emphasised that Mr Urey's actions exemplified the values of care and compassion that are central to their work. His quick response not only saved a life but also ensured that the person received the support they needed afterwards.

articles.title: New Structured Medication Review Service Launched in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A new Structured Medication Review Service has been launched in Rochdale to improve patient care and medication management.
articles.content_html:
A new Structured Medication Review Service has been launched in Rochdale. This initiative aims to enhance patient care by providing thorough assessments of individuals' medication regimens.

The service will allow healthcare professionals to review and optimise medication use, ensuring that patients receive the most appropriate treatments for their conditions.

Healthcare providers are encouraged to refer patients who may benefit from a comprehensive medication review, which could lead to improved health outcomes.

This development is expected to support local healthcare efforts and improve the overall management of medications within the community.
